content.value_statement: Enterprise Scala projects need consistent guidance for functional design, concurrency, and distributed architecture. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce practical Scala plans, reviews, and optimization advice.
actual_capabilities: Advises on Scala 3 type system features, including given, using, inline, and macros.
Guides functional programming with Cats Effect, ZIO, type classes, and immutable data patterns.
Supports distributed design with Apache Pekko, Akka, event sourcing, CQRS, and stream processing.
Recommends performance practices for JVM tuning, GraalVM, profiling, benchmarking, and memory management.
Covers testing, data access, API frameworks, build tools, CI/CD, Docker, and Kubernetes for Scala services.
limitations: It provides guidance and review support, not automatic compilation or runtime verification.
It does not include a dedicated tool or script for modifying Scala projects.
It cannot validate private infrastructure, production telemetry, or dependency versions without user-provided context.
It is most useful when the user provides code, architecture goals, or performance symptoms.

use_cases.title: Design a service architecture
use_cases.description: Plan bounded contexts, API contracts, failure handling, and event-driven workflows for a Scala microservice system.

use_cases.title: Review functional Scala code
use_cases.description: Check effect usage, error modeling, immutability, pattern matching, and type safety in production Scala code.

use_cases.title: Improve platform performance
use_cases.description: Analyze JVM behavior, Spark workloads, stream backpressure, and benchmarking plans for Scala applications.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Scala design choice
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner wants clear guidance before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the best Scala approach for [feature]. Compare functional and object-oriented options, then recommend a simple implementation path.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Scala module
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wants feedback on code quality and maintainability.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Scala module for type safety, error handling, effects, testability, and performance. Prioritize concrete changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a distributed workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Team needs a reliable architecture for production services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Scala architecture for [workflow]. Include service boundaries, messaging, consistency model, retries, observability, and failure modes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a production system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user needs performance and reliability analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Scala performance symptoms and system constraints. Propose measurement steps, likely bottlenecks, code changes, and rollout safeguards.

output_examples.input: Review a service that mixes Future, blocking database calls, and ad hoc error strings.
output: Highlights blocking risks and unclear execution context usage.
Recommends explicit error types and a consistent effect model.
Suggests tests for failure paths, timeouts, and retry behavior.

output_examples.input: Plan an event-sourced ordering service with Scala and Apache Pekko.
output: Defines aggregate boundaries, commands, events, projections, and consistency rules.
Explains shard placement, persistence choices, backpressure, and recovery behavior.
Lists verification steps for replay, idempotency, and operational monitoring.

output_examples.input: Find likely causes of high memory use in a Spark job.
output: Separates data skew, caching, shuffle pressure, serialization, and executor sizing concerns.
Recommends measurements before tuning JVM and Spark settings.
Proposes focused experiments with clear success criteria.

best_practices: Provide code snippets, dependency versions, runtime constraints, and expected behavior when requesting analysis.
Ask for tradeoffs when choosing between Cats Effect, ZIO, Future, Akka, Pekko, FS2, or Spark patterns.
Use the recommendations with compiler checks, tests, profiling data, and staged production rollout plans.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad Scala advice without a project goal, code sample, or system constraint.
Do not replace profiling, load testing, or production telemetry with general performance suggestions.
Do not mix multiple effect systems or concurrency models without documenting boundaries and migration steps.

faq.question: What Scala topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Scala 3, functional programming, effect systems, distributed systems, Spark, Akka, Pekko, APIs, testing, and JVM performance.

faq.question: Can it write Scala code?
faq.answer: It can help draft and review Scala code when the user provides requirements, constraints, and project context.

faq.question: Does it run tests or compile projects?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only. Users must run compilers, tests, linters, benchmarks, and deployment checks in their environment.

faq.question: Is it useful for legacy Akka systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Akka applications and migration considerations for Apache Pekko.

faq.question: Can it help with Spark performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest investigation steps for Spark jobs, including skew, shuffles, caching, serialization, and executor sizing.

faq.question: How should I get the best result?
faq.answer: Share the code, goal, Scala version, dependencies, runtime environment, observed behavior, and any failure or performance data.
